_comment: Accepted deltas for the proto-audit netlink layout oracle.
The oracle (nix/checks/proto-audit-netlink.nix) compares xtcp2's Go netlink
structs against the Linux kernel UAPI headers and 14 other sources, indexed
by WIRE BIT OFFSET rather than by field name. Some reported deltas are
deliberate design choices, and some are limitations of proto-audit itself;
each one is recorded here so the check can gate without being permanently
red.
Reviewed like docs/coverage-baseline.txt: an entry is a standing decision,
so adding one needs the same scrutiny as lowering a coverage floor. A delta
that is merely inconvenient does not belong here — only one that is correct.
Keys are protocol names as proto-audit reports them (see `proto-audit list`).
Each entry is matched on protocol + offset_bits + field, so a field moving
to a different offset stops being allowlisted and the check goes red again.
That is intentional: the offset is the thing being asserted.
TWO KINDS APPEAR BELOW:
kind=semantic   proto-audit's own name-based type heuristic
(src/extractors/xtcp2.rs infer_field_type) labels a field
Enum/Flags where its kernel extractor says Uint. An
annotation disagreement, not a layout one. Permanent.
kind=split      the kernel declares a C bitfield and xtcp2 unpacks it
into one Go field per member, so the two sides disagree
about where the boundaries fall while decoding the same
bytes identically. Layout-equivalent. Every split delta
comes in a PAIR — one entry per side — so they are
allowlisted in pairs; see the note below.
A third kind, kind=upstream-registry-pin, existed until the xdp2 pin moved
to 16aa7676. It recorded 11 fields proto-audit could not see because it was
reading the wrong xtcp2 struct. All 11 are gone now — 7 became agreements
and 4 turned into split pairs. Read the note below before reintroducing the
kind: a fixed upstream bug must not leave allowlist entries behind, because
they would mask a genuine future delta at the same offsets.
_note_NL_Diag_TCPInfo: WHICH SIDE IS WHICH. Every split entry below comes in a pair, and the two
halves are told apart by the field NAME, not by anything in the entry:
tcpi_*  is the KERNEL side. proto-audit's kernel extractor reads the C
declaration in linux/include/uapi/linux/tcp.h, bitfield widths
included, so it emits one field per bitfield member with the
member's real width (2, 4, 24 bits ...).
bare    is the XTCP2 side. Its extractor walks the Go struct and takes
each field's declared Go type at face value, so xtcp2's
`EcnMode uint8` reads as a whole 8-bit field starting where the
previous Go field ended. It has no way to know the decoder
unpacks that value out of a shared __u32 by hand.
Neither side is wrong about the bytes. xtcp2 deliberately unpacks packed
kernel bitfields into one Go field each — see the comment at
pkg/xtcpnl/xtcpnl_inet_diag_tcpinfo.go:256-263 — because a caller wants
`EcnMode`, not a __u32 to mask. The disagreement is about field boundaries
in the model, and it shows up as an `overlaps with:` mismatch on both
sides at once, which is why both halves need an entry.
Two bitfields in this struct produce pairs. Byte 6/7 (snd_wscale,
rcv_wscale, delivery_rate_app_limited, fastopen_client_fail) has done so
since the oracle was first run. The __u32 at [276:280] joined them when
the xdp2 pin moved to 16aa7676; that story is worth keeping:
Until that bump, xdp2's registry hardcoded the Go struct name —
`.xtcp2("TCPInfo6_10_3")` at samples/proto_audit/src/name_mapping/table.rs.
TCPInfo6_10_3 is the 248-byte struct that ends at tcpi_total_rto_time and
predates Accurate ECN, so resolve_alias() (src/extractors/xtcp2.rs:56),
which exists precisely to follow `type TCPInfo TCPInfo7_0_3`, was never
reached: the name handed to it was already concrete. All 11 AccECN fields
therefore read as MISSING FROM XTCP2 when xtcp2 was the side that had them.
They were allowlisted as kind=upstream-registry-pin and the fix went
upstream as https://github.com/randomizedcoder/xdp2/pull/11.
Measured across the bump, NL_Diag_TCPInfo goes
76/54/3/8/11  ->  80/61/3/16/0   (total/agree/type_differ/mismatch/missing)
Note what that is NOT: it is not 11 missing becoming 11 agreements. The 7
plain __u32 counters (tcpi_received_ce and the six *_e{0,1,ce}_bytes) did
become agreements and need no entry at all. The other 4 are the members of
the [276:280] bitfield, and they reappeared as 4 split PAIRS — 8 entries,
the last 8 below. Anyone repeating this exercise on another struct should
expect the same shape: fixing the registry pin converts plain fields to
agreements and converts bitfield members to split pairs.
One upstream nit remains at this rev, tracked in nix/upstream-pins.json:
extract_size_const (src/extractors/xtcp2.rs:143) builds the pattern
`{struct}SizeCst`, but xtcp2 spells these `TCPInfo7_0_3_SizeCst` with an
underscore, so no versioned size constant is ever matched and the size is
inferred from the Go field offsets — which is why `extract --source xtcp2`
now reports min_header_bytes 283 rather than 280. 283 is where the last
unpacked Go field ends, not the size of the wire struct. Harmless for this
oracle: it compares by bit offset, and min_header_bytes is a minimum.

NL_Diag_TCPInfo.reason: proto-audit's infer_field_type() sees "state" in the name and labels xtcp2's field Enum; its kernel extractor says Uint. Both agree it is 8 bits at offset 0. Annotation, not layout.
Same heuristic as tcpi_state: "state" in the name yields Enum vs the kernel's Uint. Offset and size agree.

infer_field_type() labels anything containing "options" as Flags; the kernel extractor says Uint. It IS a flags byte (TCPI_OPT_TIMESTAMPS etc., linux/include/uapi/linux/tcp.h), so the heuristic is arguably the more accurate of the two. Offset and size agree.

KERNEL side. Byte 6 is `__u8 tcpi_snd_wscale:4, tcpi_rcv_wscale:4` (linux/include/uapi/linux/tcp.h), so the kernel extractor emits a 4-bit field here. xtcp2 unpacks the two nibbles into `SndWscale uint8` and `RcvWscale uint8`, whose declared Go widths are a byte each, so this nibble reads as overlapping xtcp2's snd_wscale. Layout-equivalent; both decode byte 6 identically.
XTCP2 side of the same pair. `SndWscale uint8` is a whole byte to a Go-struct walk, so it is reported as 8 bits at 48 and overlaps both kernel nibbles. Same single root cause as tcpi_snd_wscale @48.
KERNEL side, high nibble of byte 6 (bits 4-7); see tcpi_snd_wscale @48.

KERNEL side. Byte 7 is `__u8 tcpi_delivery_rate_app_limited:1, tcpi_fastopen_client_fail:2`, so the kernel extractor emits a 1-bit field here. xtcp2's second unpacked byte-6/7 field, `RcvWscale uint8`, occupies the whole of byte 7 in a Go-struct walk, so this bit reads as overlapping it. Layout-equivalent.

XTCP2 side of the byte-7 disagreement, and the clearest illustration of why this allowlist matches on OFFSET rather than on name: `RcvWscale` is really the high nibble of byte 6, but because SndWscale ahead of it already consumed a declared byte, the Go-struct walk lands it on byte 7. The name is a byte off from what the offset says. Nothing is wrong with the decoder — it reads both nibbles out of byte 6 — only with treating declared Go widths as wire widths.
KERNEL side, bits 1-2 of byte 7; see tcpi_delivery_rate_app_limited @56.

XTCP2 side, and a phantom. Having spent a declared byte on each of SndWscale and RcvWscale, the Go-struct walk lands DeliveryRateAppLimited on byte 8 — which is really tcpi_rto, hence `overlaps with: tcpi_rto`. xtcp2's Rto is nonetheless reported correctly at 64, because its `bytes:4 [8:12]` annotation is honored, and the pcap corpus confirms it (validate-netlink grades NL_Diag_TCPInfo Gold across 8 kernel versions). Downstream of the same unpacking.
XTCP2 side, second phantom byte from the same cause; see delivery_rate_app_limited @64.

KERNEL side. The AccECN trailer ends in one `__u32` at [276:280] declared `tcpi_ecn_mode:2, tcpi_accecn_opt_seen:2, tcpi_accecn_fail_mode:4, tcpi_options2:24`, so the kernel extractor emits a 2-bit field here. xtcp2 unpacks all four into separate Go fields (pkg/xtcpnl/xtcpnl_inet_diag_tcpinfo.go:260-263), the first of which, `EcnMode uint8`, reads as a whole byte — hence `overlaps with: ecn_mode`. Same class as tcpi_snd_wscale @48; appeared when the xdp2 pin moved to 16aa7676 and proto-audit could finally see the trailer at all.

XTCP2 side of the pair at 2208. `EcnMode uint8` is a byte to a Go-struct walk, so it is reported as 8 bits at 2208 and overlaps three kernel bitfield members at once (tcpi_ecn_mode, tcpi_accecn_opt_seen, tcpi_accecn_fail_mode). The decoder masks bits 0-1 out of the shared __u32 and is correct.
KERNEL side, bits 2-3 of the [276:280] __u32; see tcpi_ecn_mode @2208.
KERNEL side, bits 4-7 of the [276:280] __u32; see tcpi_ecn_mode @2208.

XTCP2 side. `AccecnOptSeen uint8` is xtcp2's second unpacked field, so the Go-struct walk puts it at byte 277 while the kernel puts tcpi_options2 there. Off by a byte for the same reason rcv_wscale @56 is; the decoder reads bits 2-3 of the shared __u32.
KERNEL side, bits 8-31 of the [276:280] __u32 — the last 24 bits of the struct; see tcpi_ecn_mode @2208.
XTCP2 side. `AccecnFailMode uint8` lands on byte 278 in a Go-struct walk; the decoder reads bits 4-7 of the shared __u32. See accecn_opt_seen @2216.

XTCP2 side, and the one entry that runs off the end of the struct: `Options2 uint32` is four declared bytes starting at byte 279, so a Go-struct walk puts it at [279:283] — past the 280-byte wire struct. That overrun is also why `extract --source xtcp2 --proto NL_Diag_TCPInfo` reports min_header_bytes 283. The decoder reads bits 8-31 of the __u32 at [276:280] and stops at 280; the corpus confirms it. Same phantom shape as fastopen_client_fail @72.
